summary.en: Choose Singleton, Factory, Strategy or Observer by its problem and tradeoffs.
summary.bn: সমস্যা ও সীমাবদ্ধতা বুঝে Singleton, Factory, Strategy বা Observer বেছে নাও।

notes: No deprecated Observable/Observer helper is used. The eager Singleton relies on ordinary class initialization in Java 17.

sections.title: Name a recurring problem before choosing its solution
Recognize the contract and the collaborating roles
Match each pattern to its pressure and cost
Run one bounded design for each role
A shared accessor is also a shared dependency
Keep object selection outside stable consumers
Subscriptions create obligations beyond a callback method
Recognize familiar roles in Java APIs
Check the motivation before adding a pattern
Use current contracts without deprecated helpers
State the problem, roles and consequence

examples.title: Singleton: one immutable settings object
examples.explanationHtml: Both requests return the same instance within this loaded class. Eager static initialization safely constructs immutable settings.

examples.title: Factory: centralize construction choices
examples.explanationHtml: Callers receive the Notice contract. The factory chooses concrete classes; its accepted kind domain here is zero or one.

examples.title: Strategy: inject a fare algorithm
examples.explanationHtml: Ticket owns the context of a fare request. Rate is a replaceable algorithm chosen by the caller.

examples.title: Observer: notify two registered displays
examples.explanationHtml: publish synchronously visits listeners in registration order. This bounded demonstration allows two listeners and does not mutate registration during notification.

practice.title: Factory-selected receipt
practice.statementHtml: Read kind (0 exam, 1 lab) and quantity (0..20). Use NoticeFactory to create one Notice. Print its text quantity times, one per line; print nothing for zero.
hints: Construction belongs in the factory; printing uses Notice.

practice.title: Observer total and latest
practice.statementHtml: Read n (0..20) then n seat counts (0..100). Board publishes each count to a SumListener and LatestListener. Print their sum and latest value separated by one space; latest is zero with no events.
hints: Observer state belongs to the individual listener.

practice.title: Avoid a mutable global registry
practice.statementHtml: An application makes every course register a Singleton. Explain a consequence and offer an alternative.
practice.answerHtml: A global mutable register couples unrelated users and tests to one shared state. Construct a register per application or use case, then inject it into consumers. Singleton is suitable only when the single-instance lifetime is a real requirement, not a shortcut for passing references.
hints: Ask who owns the state and when it should reset.

practice.title: Factory or Strategy?
practice.statementHtml: A new scholarship type needs a different object at creation. A running checkout needs a replaceable discount calculation. Choose a pattern for each.
practice.answerHtml: A factory centralizes scholarship object construction behind a return contract. Strategy makes checkout delegate discount calculation to a policy object. A factory may create a strategy, but the construction role and the algorithm role remain different.

practice.title: Observer lifecycle
practice.statementHtml: A display is closed but stays registered with a long-lived board. Explain the risk and design an unsubscribe operation.
practice.answerHtml: The board may retain the display and continue sending events, keeping it reachable and doing unwanted work. Return a registration handle or offer unsubscribe(listener). Define duplicate, removal and in-progress notification rules. A snapshot of registrations can make changes during notification predictable.
hints: Subscriptions need an explicit end as well as a start.

quiz.prompt: Do two Singleton accessor calls return one object?
quiz.explanation: The accessor returns the static INSTANCE each time.

quiz.prompt: Which concrete notice does the factory select for kind one?
quiz.explanation: Kind one selects LabNotice, whose text is Lab.

quiz.prompt: How does Strategy change the fare for distance seven?
quiz.explanation: ReducedRate multiplies the distance by two.

quiz.prompt: What order do synchronous observer callbacks use here?
quiz.explanation: The bounded array is traversed from the first registered display to the second.

quiz.prompt: Which problem is a factory intended to address?
quiz.explanation: Factories isolate construction choices behind an agreed return contract.
options: Centralizing how concrete objects are chosen and created

quiz.explanation: The context keeps the algorithm contract and forwards work to the supplied implementation.
options: A context delegating a varying algorithm

quiz.prompt: What is a cost of Singleton with mutable state?
quiz.explanation: Global access can hide dependencies and make tests influence one another.
options: Hidden shared state and difficult isolation

quiz.prompt: What must an Observer design define beyond notification?
quiz.explanation: Registration removal, ordering and failures affect correctness and resource use.
options: A new superclass for every event
Subscription lifetime and callback failure policy

quiz.prompt: Which Java library capability resembles Strategy?
quiz.explanation: A comparator supplies a replaceable ordering algorithm to a sorting context.

quiz.prompt: Which Java API commonly uses Observer-style callbacks?
quiz.explanation: Registered listeners receive event callbacks. Swing events have their own event-thread rules.

quiz.prompt: Why avoid java.util.Observable in new examples?
quiz.explanation: Use a focused listener contract or an appropriate modern event API instead of the deprecated helper.
options: It cannot compile on any Java release
It is deprecated and has design limitations

quiz.prompt: What does this eager Singleton guarantee without extra machinery?
quiz.explanation: Class-loader boundaries and advanced construction mechanisms need separate consideration.
options: One instance across every JVM process
Universal protection against reflection and serialization tricks
One instance through its accessor per loaded Settings class

keyPoints.en: A pattern names a recurring design problem and a solution shape.
keyPoints.bn: প্যাটার্ন বারবার দেখা ডিজাইন সমস্যার সমাধানের ধরনকে নাম দেয়।

keyPoints.en: Singleton centralizes lifetime but can hide shared dependencies.
keyPoints.bn: Singleton জীবনকাল কেন্দ্রীভূত করে, তবে শেয়ার করা নির্ভরতা আড়াল করতে পারে।

keyPoints.en: Factories choose construction while strategies choose algorithms.
keyPoints.bn: Factory অবজেক্ট তৈরি নির্বাচন করে, Strategy অ্যালগরিদম নির্বাচন করে।

keyPoints.en: Observers require explicit ordering and subscription policies.
keyPoints.bn: Observer-এ ক্রম এবং সাবস্ক্রিপশনের নিয়ম স্পষ্ট করতে হয়।

keyPoints.en: Choose a pattern only when its tradeoffs fit the problem.
keyPoints.bn: সমস্যার সঙ্গে সুবিধা ও খরচ মিললেই প্যাটার্ন বেছে নাও।

examQuestions.question: Compare Factory and Strategy using a fee system.
examQuestions.answerHtml: A factory creates an appropriate FeePolicy from a validated choice. Strategy lets Checkout delegate its calculation to FeePolicy. The factory can build the strategy, but Checkout should depend on the algorithm contract rather than concrete policy names.

examQuestions.question: Design an Observer seat board and state its consequences.
examQuestions.answerHtml:
SeatBoard --> Listener
              ^
              | implements
           GateDisplay

The board registers listeners and publishes seat changes through changed(seats). Specify ordering, duplicate registration, removal, callback failures and reentrant updates. Synchronous callbacks are simple but a slow listener delays publishing.

examQuestions.question: Explain an eager Singleton’s thread-safety scope and testing cost.
examQuestions.answerHtml: Static class initialization safely publishes the eagerly created instance. That does not make future mutable fields thread-safe. The same loaded class shares the instance, so mutable state can couple tests. Injecting an ordinary instance often gives clearer lifetime control.

examQuestions.question: Identify library examples of Strategy, Factory and Observer without using deprecated helpers.
examQuestions.answerHtml: Comparator supplies Strategy-like ordering. NumberFormat.getIntegerInstance is a factory-style creation method. Swing ActionListener is an Observer-style event callback. These examples illustrate roles rather than claiming that every factory-style method implements the full Factory Method pattern.
